property_summary: The stored owner address equals the contract's owner() getter return value.
The test asserts that the provided expectedOwner equals c.owner() (got == expectedOwner).
The test asserts that the address returned by c.owner() equals the provided expectedOwner.
The test checks that the contract's owner() view returns the provided expectedOwner (assert(got == expectedOwner)).
The test asserts that c.owner() (got) equals the provided expectedOwner.

For every input, the reference contract's owner() returns the exact stored owner (the address set at construction), whereas the mutant returns a different deterministically-derived address; thus owner() should equal the originally stored owner for all calls — the mutant violates this for some inputs.

For any caller the reference contract's owner() always returns the stored owner address set at construction/transferOwnership, whereas the mutant returns the caller (msg.sender) so for some caller addresses the returned value differs.

For any caller, the deployed contract's owner() must return the deployer address (the Context _msgSender() at construction); the mutant that always returns address(0) violates this for any input where deployer != address(0).

For all callers, reference contract's owner() returns the stored owner address (the account set at construction or via transferOwnership), whereas the mutant returns tx.origin and thus can differ for calls made via contracts — the test fuzzes a caller address and asserts owner() equals the stored owner when called from that caller (via an external call), which the mutant will violate for some caller addresses.

For any caller (EOA or contract), calling owner() via a direct external CALL should return the originally stored owner address (set at construction); the mutant that returns tx.origin will return a different address when called through an intermediate contract (tx.origin != original owner), so some contract-callers will make the mutant diverge.

For any caller (EOA or contract) invoking owner() on C, the returned address always equals the originally stored owner (the deployer); the mutant returning tx.origin can differ when owner() is called through an intermediate contract (tx.origin ≠ stored owner), so the property is violated for some contract-callers.

For every caller (EOA or contract) that calls C.owner(), the reference contract returns the stored owner address (the deployer set in constructor); the mutant that returns tx.origin can return a different address when the caller is a contract that forwards the call and sets tx.origin to an EOA different from the stored owner, so there exist caller-contract / tx.origin pairs that make the mutant disagree.

For any externally-observable call context (any msg.sender and any caller contract), calling C.owner() via a low-level call initiated by a caller contract returns the originally stored owner (the deployer) — the mutant returns tx.origin instead and thus will differ when the caller contract is invoked by an EOA different from the deployer; the test fuzzes the EOA caller so the mutant fails for some EOA values.
For every input the reference contract's owner() returns the externally set owner (the deployer), never the contract's own address; the mutant breaks this because it returns address(this) instead.
